findings.summary: Alt+Ctrl-d (ESC 0x04, one key) to an OMP pane is split: the ESC is forwarded alone and the 0x04 held; a second press sends another lone ESC and re-holds, so the key can never be delivered and each press sends a bare Esc (which OMP uses to interrupt/cancel). Repro: focus manager, type b'\x1b\x04' -> input b'\x1b'; twice -> b'\x1b\x1b'.

HELP_LINES has 30 lines and the overlay shows rows-4 of them; the new Ctrl-d confirmation line is the last one, so it is cut off on terminals shorter than 34 rows (e.g. 24/30-row panes in herdr/tmux).

The guard matches only raw 0x04. If an outer terminal is configured to send modified keys as CSI-u / modifyOtherKeys (\x1b[100;5u, \x1b[27;5;100~) the Ctrl-d reaches OMP unguarded. The UI itself never enables these modes, so this is outside the C-D61 'raw 0x04' scope; noted for Root.
Mouse wheel / click on the same pane do not cancel a held Ctrl-d (worker-02 design); tested as documented behaviour, not as a defect.
